_comment: A component set is one specific bill of materials: this load cell, this
display, this board, this battery. Selecting a set overrides the component
parameters in params/default.json, and because the enclosure is derived
from its contents, the case resizes itself to suit.
This is the layer that makes the model genuinely reusable. Changing to a
different display or a bigger battery is a one-line change here, not a

v1_measured.description: Confirmed BOM from the build log at buildlog.pravton.com/projects/bottle-feed-logger. Enclosure features are measured from the V1 meshes; module envelopes still need calipers.
notes: Confirmed BOM: ESP32 DevKit V1, 1 kg bar load cell, HX711, SSD1306 0.96in OLED,
two momentary push buttons, USB powered. All mounted on a HALF-SIZE (400 point)
breadboard, not as loose modules: see the build log gallery.
The OLED is mounted PORTRAIT: V1's aperture is 14 x 26, taller than wide.
breadboard_x / breadboard_y / breadboard_h / component_stack_h are the
measurements that now matter most: the cavity is sized from the breadboard.

display_bezel is gone: V1 recessed the OLED module into the lid underside, but a blind pocket there gives the module nowhere to enter from. V2 has a plain through aperture and retains the module some other way.

TO_CONFIRM.description: Empty set. Everything falls through to the placeholders in default.json.

_measurement_protocol: L x W x H     maximum envelope including connectors and any heatsink
mounting      hole pattern, hole diameter, boss height needed
cable exit    which face, and how much bend radius the loom needs
For the load cell specifically, also record:
rated capacity        must exceed load_capacity with margin
full-scale deflection sets the clearance gap under the free end
bar length            sets pan offset from the fixed end
thread size and depth on both ends; the free end is often a different
size from the fixed end, which is easy to miss
